# Krutrim Sandbox — for AI agents

Isolated Linux machines created from one API call, used, and destroyed. This file is
written for an agent to act on directly: everything needed to create a sandbox, run work
in it and clean up is below, so no further fetching is required.

Everything here was measured against production in In-Bangalore-1 on 2026-10-17 at
`template-v1.2.1`. Numbers go stale; the constraints rarely do.

## Authentication

Create a key in the Krutrim Cloud console at https://cloud.olakrutrim.com under
**Administration -> API keys -> Create API Key**. One key covers Sandbox, MCP, Models,
CLI and the SDK.

Three environment variable names are in circulation. Only one works for this SDK:

| Variable | Read by |
|---|---|
| `KRUTRIMCLIENT_API_KEY` | `krutrim-client` (the Python SDK) — **use this one** |
| `KRUTRIM_API_KEY` | `krutrim-mcp-server` only |
| `krutrim_client_API_KEY` | nothing — appeared in older README text |

Setting the wrong one leaves `api_key` as `None` and fails on the first request with an
error that looks like a bad key rather than a bad variable name.

## Minimal working example

```python
pip install krutrim-client
export KRUTRIMCLIENT_API_KEY="<your API key>"
```

Create your own key in the console (above) and keep it wherever your environment keeps
secrets. Nothing in the SDK expects a particular file or location — it reads the
environment variable and nothing else.

```python
from krutrim_client import KrutrimClient

c = KrutrimClient()

with c.sandbox.create(
    sandbox_name="my-job",          # DNS-1035, 28 characters or fewer
    region="In-Bangalore-1",        # or In-Hyderabad-1
    flavor_name="sandbox-small",
    timeout=900,                    # TTL in seconds; a dead-man's switch
    image_uri="ghcr.io/ola-krutrim/sandbox-rust:template-v1.2.1",
) as sb:
    out = sb.run_command("cargo --version")   # timeout must be <= 270
    print(out.stdout, out.exit_code)
    sb.files.write("/app/result.txt", "data") # paths are rooted at /app
    print(sb.files.read("/app/result.txt"))
# sandbox destroyed here, including if the body raised
```

Use the context-manager form. A sandbox bills until it is destroyed or its TTL reaps it.

## Hard constraints an agent will hit

| Constraint | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `sandbox_name` | DNS-1035, **<= 28 characters**. Longer returns HTTP 400 from the service. Truncate *then* strip trailing hyphens — `"browser-playwright"[:8]` is `"browser-"`, which is invalid. |
| `run_command(timeout=)` | **1-270 seconds**, enforced client-side. Longer work must run detached inside the sandbox with a marker file polled by short commands. |
| Create rate | Unspaced bursts degrade, then fail as a gateway `403` surfaced as `PermissionDeniedError` — not a 429, no `Retry-After`, so ordinary retry logic will not retry it. **Space creates by ~8 s.** |
| Files API | Every path is rooted at `SANDBOX_BASE_DIR` (`/app`). `files.write("/tmp/x")` lands at `/app/tmp/x` while the response reports `/tmp/x`. Write under `/app`. |
| TTL | 60 s to 7 days. No pause, no resume, no snapshot. |
| Runtime user | Containers currently start as **uid 0** regardless of the image's `USER`. |
| Egress policy | `allow_internet_access` and the allowlist parameters are accepted, echoed with HTTP 200, and **not enforced** — they fail **open**. Not a security boundary. |
| Outbound IP | All sandboxes in a region share **one** NAT address. Volume crawling is capped and a block affects every tenant. |

## Timing and cost

- Bare sandbox, create to usable: **~1.6 s**
- A template adds **~0.8 s**, and this does **not** scale with image size
- First pull of an image into a region: 8-71 s depending on size, **once**
- A full repo clone-and-build on `sandbox-large`: about **Rs 0.09**

Do not budget from cold-create times; they are a one-time per-image-per-region cost.

## Templates

All public and anonymously pullable at
`ghcr.io/ola-krutrim/sandbox-<name>:template-v1.2.1`. Each version below was read from
the tool running inside a sandbox created from that published image.

## MCP

`krutrim-mcp-server` exposes 160 tools, 19 of them sandbox operations
(`create_sandbox`, `delete_sandbox`, `list_sandbox_templates`, `set_sandbox_ttl` and
others). It reads `KRUTRIM_API_KEY`, not the SDK variable.
